blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Chapter 12 (Nitrogen and Sulfur), arranged by the chapter's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each answer is a short model answer; small numericals show the working, and a comparison is answered as a table.

blocks.prompt: 1 How is nitrogen gas prepared in the laboratory? Give the balanced equation.
blocks.explanation: Nitrogen is generated by slowly heating a solution of ammonium nitrite: NH₄NO₂(aq) → N₂(g) + 2H₂O(l) (on heating). Two H₂O are needed to balance 4 H and 2 O.

book_ref.quote: nitrogen can be generated by slowly heating a solution of ammonium nitrite

blocks.prompt: 2 What mass of nitrogen is obtained by heating 6.4 g of ammonium nitrite? (NH₄NO₂ = 64.05 g mol⁻¹, N₂ = 28.02 g mol⁻¹)
blocks.explanation: NH₄NO₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O, so 1 mol gives 1 mol N₂. n = 6.4 ÷ 64.05 = 0.0999 mol; mass of N₂ = 0.0999 × 28.02 = 2.80 g.

book_ref.quote: The balanced equation is NH₄NO₂(aq) → N₂(g) + 2H₂O(l).

blocks.prompt: 3 Why is the bond in the N₂ molecule nonpolar?
blocks.explanation: Both atoms are nitrogen, so the electronegativity difference is zero. The bonded electrons are shared equally between the two atoms, so the triple bond is nonpolar.

book_ref.quote: This causes equal sharing of the three bonded electrons between the two atoms

blocks.prompt: 4 What does the bond enthalpy of +944 kJ mol⁻¹ of N≡N tell us about nitrogen?
blocks.explanation: The triple bond is very strong; high energy is needed to break it before new bonds can form. Hence N₂ is very unreactive.

book_ref.quote: High energy is required to break this bond to form new bonds

blocks.prompt: 5 Give two uses of nitrogen as an inert gas.
blocks.explanation: (i) Blankets of nitrogen on ships carrying hydrocarbons or edible oils protect them from oxygen and moisture. (ii) In the laboratory it provides an inert atmosphere for reactions that need one.

book_ref.quote: it is crucial to utilize blankets of Nitrogen or any other inert gas on ships

blocks.prompt: 6 Name the industrial process for ammonia and write its equation. What is the main use of ammonia?
blocks.explanation: Haber-Bosch process: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) (on heating). Ammonia is mainly used as a fertilizer.

book_ref.quote: It is prepared industrially by Haber-Bosch process

blocks.prompt: 7 Show with an equation that ammonia is a Lowry-Brønsted base.
blocks.explanation: A Lowry-Brønsted base accepts a proton. Ammonia accepts H⁺ from an acid to form ammonium: NH₃(aq) + H⁺(aq) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq).

book_ref.quote: Ammonia behaves as a Lowry-Brønsted base by accepting a proton

blocks.prompt: 8 Write the equilibrium set up when ammonia dissolves in water and name the ions formed.
blocks.explanation: NH₃(aq) + H₂O(l) ⇌ NH₄⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq), Kb = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵. The ions are ammonium (NH₄⁺) and hydroxide (OH⁻); the solution is called ammonium hydroxide.

book_ref.quote: equilibrium is established between ammonia molecules and ammonium ions in the solution

blocks.prompt: 9 Why does the shape change when ammonia forms the ammonium ion?
blocks.explanation: NH₃ is pyramidal because of the lone pair on nitrogen. When nitrogen uses this lone pair to bond H⁺, there is no lone pair left and NH₄⁺ becomes tetrahedral with four equal bonds.

book_ref.quote: Ammonia molecule has pyramidal shape due to lone pair of nitrogen

blocks.prompt: 10 Differentiate between NH₃ and NH₄⁺ with respect to shape and lone pair.
blocks.explanation: See the table.

book_ref.quote: this ion adopts a tetrahedral shape

rows: Lone pair used to bond H⁺; no lone pair
Four N–H bonds of equal length and strength

blocks.text: 12.2.3 Synthesis of ammonia from ammonium salts

blocks.prompt: 11 Write the balanced equation for heating ammonium chloride with calcium hydroxide. Which salt forms?
blocks.explanation: 2NH₄Cl(s) + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O(l) + 2NH₃(g). The salt is calcium chloride, CaCl₂ (no sodium is present, so NaCl cannot form).

book_ref.quote: There is no sodium in the reactants, so NaCl cannot form

blocks.prompt: 12 In the preparation of ammonia from an ammonium salt and a base, identify the acid and the base.
blocks.explanation: It is an acid-base reaction: NH₄⁺ is the acid (donates H⁺) and OH⁻ is the base (accepts H⁺). Ammonia gas is displaced, and a salt and water are formed.

book_ref.quote: while OH⁻ acts as a base by accepting H⁺ ions

blocks.prompt: 13 How is the ammonium ion identified in salt analysis?
blocks.explanation: The salt is heated with a base. If a gas with a pungent smell is released that turns moistened red litmus paper blue (ammonia), ammonium is present.

book_ref.quote: It is commonly used to identify ammonium in salt analysis

blocks.prompt: 14 Why is the test tube clamped sloping slightly downwards towards its mouth when ammonia is prepared from a heated solid mixture?
blocks.explanation: Water is formed in the reaction. With the mouth slightly lower, the water does not run back onto the hot glass, which could crack the tube.

book_ref.quote: The tube should slope slightly downwards towards its mouth

blocks.prompt: 15 Why is the formula of ammonium nitrate NH₄NO₃ and not (NH₄)₂NO₃?
blocks.explanation: Ammonium ion has charge +1 and nitrate ion has charge −1. One NH₄⁺ balances one NO₃⁻, so the neutral formula is NH₄NO₃.

book_ref.quote: Ammonium nitrate is NH₄NO₃, not (NH₄)₂NO₃

blocks.prompt: 16 What is meant by NOₓ? Name the oxides of nitrogen given in the chapter.
blocks.explanation: NO and NO₂ together are called NOₓ. The oxides of nitrogen are NO, N₂O, NO₂, N₂O₄ and N₂O₅, with oxidation states from +1 to +5.

book_ref.quote: NO and NO₂ are collectively called as NOₓ

blocks.prompt: 17 Why is NO paramagnetic while its dimer N₂O₂ is diamagnetic?
blocks.explanation: NO has 11 valence electrons (5 + 6), an odd number, so one electron is unpaired: NO is paramagnetic. In N₂O₂ the two odd electrons pair up, so the dimer is diamagnetic.

book_ref.quote: NO has 11 valence electrons: N=O with an unpaired electron on N

blocks.prompt: 18 What is the effect of cooling and heating on the equilibrium 2NO₂ ⇌ N₂O₄?
blocks.explanation: Cooling shifts the equilibrium forward to colourless N₂O₄, so the brown colour fades. Heating shifts it back to brown NO₂, so the colour deepens.

book_ref.quote: 2NO₂ (Brown) ⇌ N₂O₄ (Colourless): Cool →, ← Heat

blocks.prompt: 19 Give two properties and two uses of nitrous oxide (N₂O).
blocks.explanation: Properties: colourless, sweet-smelling, water-soluble neutral gas that helps in combustion. Uses: dental anaesthetic (laughing gas) and propellant for whipped ice cream (also synthesis of NaN₃).

book_ref.quote: Colourless gas, water-soluble, neutral, sweet smelling, helps in combustion

blocks.prompt: 20 Calculate the oxidation state of nitrogen in N₂O, NO₂ and N₂O₅.

book_ref.quote: Nitrogen dioxide/Nitrogen peroxide, Nitrogen tetraoxide NO₂, N₂O₄

blocks.prompt: 21 What are azane and azanium? From where are these names derived?
blocks.explanation: Azane is the IUPAC-recommended name for ammonia and azanium for ammonium. They come from Azote, a Greek name for nitrogen meaning 'no life'; they are used in naming derivatives such as sodium azide (NaN₃).

book_ref.quote: These names have been derived from Azote

blocks.prompt: 22 Differentiate between natural and anthropogenic sources of NOₓ.
blocks.explanation: See the table.

book_ref.quote: Here are the main categories of NOₓ sources

rows: Lightning: N₂ and O₂ of air react to give NO
Combustion of fossil fuels in vehicles

blocks.prompt: 23 What is photochemical smog? Why is it called oxidising?
blocks.explanation: Photochemical (Los Angeles) smog forms in the atmosphere from NOₓ and volatile organic compounds in sunlight. It contains photochemical oxidants such as NO₂, ozone and PANs that oxidise compounds in the atmosphere, so it is oxidising.

book_ref.quote: Photochemical smog (Los Angeles smog) forms in the atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 24 Differentiate between photochemical smog and classical smog.
blocks.explanation: See the table.

book_ref.quote: Photochemical smog is becoming more common than classical smog

rows: Forms from NOₓ and VOCs in sunlight
Becoming less common than photochemical smog

blocks.prompt: 25 Name the components of Lahore smog.
blocks.explanation: Lahore smog consists of volatile organic compounds (VOCs), NOₓ, ground-level ozone (O₃), particulate matter PM2.5, CO and SO₂.

book_ref.quote: Lahore smog consists of volatile organic compounds

blocks.prompt: 26 How does sunlight lead to the formation of ozone from NO₂? Give the equations.
blocks.explanation: Sunlight splits NO₂: NO₂(g) → NO(g) + O(g) (hν). The oxygen atom joins O₂: O(g) + O₂(g) → O₃(g).

book_ref.quote: NOₓ and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the sunlight

blocks.prompt: 27 What are PANs? What is the R group in peroxyacetyl nitrate?
blocks.explanation: PANs (peroxyacyl nitrates), RC(O)OONO₂, are photochemical oxidants formed from NOₓ in smog. In peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) the R group is CH₃; other hydrocarbon chains may also be present.

book_ref.quote: PAN is one of the members of peroxyacyl nitrates

blocks.prompt: 28 What are the roles of the hydroxyl radical and of oxygen in the formation of PAN?
blocks.explanation: The hydroxyl radical reacts with the aldehyde to produce an acyl radical. Oxygen then converts the acyl radical into a peroxyacyl radical, which reacts with NO₂ to give PAN.

book_ref.quote: The aldehyde then reacts with hydroxyl radical to produce acyl radical

blocks.prompt: 29 Why are the channels of a catalytic converter coated with alumina, and which metals are dispersed on it?
blocks.explanation: The alumina layer provides a high surface area. Noble metals Pt (platinum), Pd (palladium) and Rh (rhodium) are dispersed on it to catalyse the redox reactions.

book_ref.quote: Its inner channels have a layer of alumina to provide a high surface area

blocks.prompt: 30 Write the reduction reaction of nitric oxide in a catalytic converter and name its catalyst.
blocks.explanation: 2NO(g) + 2CO(g) → N₂(g) + 2CO₂(g), catalyst Pt/Rh (platinum/rhodium). NO is reduced to N₂ while CO is oxidised to CO₂.

book_ref.quote: ‘Rd’ is not the symbol of any element

blocks.prompt: 31 Write the oxidation reactions of carbon monoxide and of a hydrocarbon (C₂H₄) in a catalytic converter.
blocks.explanation: 2CO(g) + O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) and 2C₂H₄ + 6O₂(g) → 4CO₂(g) + 4H₂O(g), both catalysed by Pt/Rh.

book_ref.quote: should be Rh: the catalyst is Pt/Rh

blocks.prompt: 32 Differentiate between nitrification and denitrification with respect to the conditions and the change of nitrogen.
blocks.explanation: See the table.

book_ref.quote: Nitrification and denitrification are the two phases of the nitrogen cycle

blocks.prompt: 33 Write the two steps of nitrification as equations.
blocks.explanation: Step 1: 2NH₄⁺(aq) + 3O₂(aq) → 2NO₂⁻(aq) + 4H⁺(aq) + 2H₂O(l). Step 2: 2NO₂⁻(aq) + O₂(aq) → 2NO₃⁻(aq).

book_ref.quote: 2NH₄¹⁺(aq) + 3O₂(aq) → 2NO₂¹⁻(aq) + 4H⁺(aq) + 2H₂O(l)

blocks.prompt: 34 Why is denitrification called a reduction of nitrogen? Give the equation.
blocks.explanation: 2NO₃⁻(aq) + 10e⁻ + 12H⁺(aq) → N₂(g) + 6H₂O(l). Nitrogen gains electrons: its oxidation state falls from +5 in NO₃⁻ to 0 in N₂, so it is reduced.

book_ref.quote: 2NO₃¹⁻(aq) + 10e⁻ + 12H⁺(aq) → N₂(g) + 6H₂O(l)

blocks.prompt: 35 Why are nitrification and denitrification important?
blocks.explanation: Nitrification gives nitrites and nitrates that plants absorb, since they cannot assimilate N₂ directly. Denitrification returns N₂ to the atmosphere. Together they are used in wastewater treatment to remove nitrogen.

book_ref.quote: These two processes are also involved in the wastewater treatment to remove nitrogen

blocks.prompt: 36 Give the group, family name, electronic configuration and common oxidation states of sulfur.
blocks.explanation: Sulfur is in group 16, the chalcogen family. Configuration [Ne] 3s² 3p⁴ (atomic number 16). Common oxidation states +4 and +6.

book_ref.quote: Sulfur is a member of group 16 which is also called the Chalcogen family

blocks.prompt: 37 What is catenation? Why does sulfur show it?
blocks.explanation: Catenation is the linking of atoms of the same element into larger molecules and structures. Sulfur forms single bonds with other S atoms instead of double bonds (poor orbital overlap), so it builds chains and rings such as the crown-shaped S₈.

book_ref.quote: it forms larger molecules and structures through a process called catenation

blocks.prompt: 38 List the oxidation states of sulfur. How are they related to its electronic configuration?
blocks.explanation: Sulfur shows −2, 0, +2, +4 and +6. In Figure 12.8 the oxidation state is determined by the number of unpaired electrons available for bonding in its electronic configuration.

book_ref.quote: the oxidation state is determined by the number of unpaired electrons

blocks.prompt: 39 Why does sulfur burn to SO₂ rather than SO₃ under standard conditions?
blocks.explanation: Under standard conditions sulfur and oxygen give SO₂ (+4). Forming SO₃ (+6) requires high energy, so SO₃ needs a higher temperature and a catalyst.

book_ref.quote: However, to form sulfur trioxide (SO₃) with an oxidation state of +6, high energy is required

blocks.text: 12.9 Stability of the oxidation states of sulfur

blocks.prompt: 40 What is a Frost diagram?
blocks.explanation: A Frost diagram of an element X is a plot of nE° against oxidation state (n) for the couple X(n)/X(0). It shows the relative stabilities of the oxidation states at pH = 0 and pH = 14.

book_ref.quote: is a plot of nE⁰ vs oxidation state (n)

blocks.prompt: 41 Give the relation between ΔG° and nE° used in a Frost diagram and name the symbols.
blocks.explanation: −ΔG° = nFE°, or −ΔG°/F = nE°. E° = standard reduction potential, F = Faraday constant, n = number of electrons transferred in the redox half reaction.

book_ref.quote: Here E⁰ is the standard reduction potential

blocks.prompt: 42 How does a Frost diagram show the stable state, a good oxidising agent and a good reducing agent?
blocks.explanation: The most stable oxidation state lies at the lowest position (lowest nE°, most negative ΔG°). A couple with a more positive slope is a good oxidising agent; one with a more negative slope is a good reducing agent.

book_ref.quote: a couple with a more negative slope is a good reducing agent

blocks.prompt: 43 For a couple X(n)/X(0) of an element X, n = 4 and E° = +0.30 V. Find nE° and ΔG°. (F = 96485 C mol⁻¹)

book_ref.quote: F is the Faraday constant and n is the number of transferred electrons

blocks.prompt: 44 Why does sulfur tarnish silver? Give the equation.
blocks.explanation: Silver has lower electronegativity than sulfur, so sulfur acts as an oxidizing agent and forms a coating of silver sulfide: 2Ag(s) + S(s) → Ag₂S(s).

book_ref.quote: It tarnishes Ag, Cu, and Zn by forming a coating of metal sulfide

blocks.prompt: 45 What is formed when potassium cyanide is heated with sulfur? Give one use of the product.
blocks.explanation: KCN(s) + S(s) → KSCN(s) (on heating). Thiocyanate, a pseudohalide, is used to analyse Fe³⁺.

book_ref.quote: Sulfur converts cyanide into thiocyanate which is also known as pseudohalide

blocks.prompt: 46 Write the reaction of sulfur with nitric acid. What happens to sulfur in it?
blocks.explanation: S(s) + 6HNO₃(l) → H₂SO₄(l) + 6NO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l). Sulfur is oxidised from 0 to +6 (in H₂SO₄); nitric acid is reduced to NO₂.

book_ref.quote: Sulfur can be oxidised by nitric acid to produce NO₂ and H₂SO₄

blocks.prompt: 47 How is sulfur hexafluoride formed, and why is it used in electric devices?
blocks.explanation: Sulfur reacts directly with fluorine: S(s) + 3F₂(g) → SF₆(g). SF₆ is a very unreactive gas, so it is used as an insulator gas in electric devices.

book_ref.quote: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF₆) is a gas and is very unreactive

blocks.prompt: 48 Find the oxidation state of sulfur in S₂Cl₂ and in SCl₂ (Cl = −1).
blocks.explanation: S₂Cl₂: 2x + 2(−1) = 0, x = +1. SCl₂: x + 2(−1) = 0, x = +2. S₂Cl₂ is a yellow liquid and SCl₂ a red liquid.

book_ref.quote: which further reacts with Cl₂ to form SCl₂ (red liquid)

blocks.prompt: 49 How is sulfur restored to soils depleted in sulfate?
blocks.explanation: By applying sulfur-containing N/P fertilizers or sulfur-coated fertilizers such as sulfur-coated urea; gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) is also used. Soil components and microbes convert elemental sulfur into soluble forms for plants.

book_ref.quote: sulfur can be restored in soil by applying sulfur containing N/P fertilizers

blocks.prompt: 50 Calculate the mass of each component in 250 g of gunpowder.
blocks.explanation: Gunpowder is 75 % KNO₃, 15 % charcoal and 10 % sulfur. KNO₃ = 0.75 × 250 = 187.5 g; charcoal = 0.15 × 250 = 37.5 g; sulfur = 0.10 × 250 = 25.0 g.

book_ref.quote: Gun powder is a coarse blend of 75% potassium nitrate

blocks.prompt: 51 Using the burning equation of gunpowder, find the moles of gas formed from 2.0 mol of KNO₃.
blocks.explanation: 10KNO₃ + 3S + 8C → 2K₂CO₃ + 3K₂SO₄ + 6CO₂ + 5N₂: 10 mol KNO₃ give 6 + 5 = 11 mol gas. For 2.0 mol: 2.0 × 11/10 = 2.2 mol gas (CO₂ + N₂).

book_ref.quote: Charcoal carbon is the main fuel, nitrate is the oxidiser

blocks.text: 12.12 Role of sulfur in the organic synthesis of drugs, dyes and fragrances

blocks.prompt: 52 Name four functional groups that contain carbon-sulfur bonds.
blocks.explanation: Thiols (mercaptans), thioethers, sulfoxides and sulfones. Such compounds have biological, pharmaceutical and material properties.

book_ref.quote: Carbon-Sulfur bonds are prevalent in a wide range of compounds

blocks.prompt: 53 What are sulfa drugs? Are penicillins sulfa drugs?
blocks.explanation: Sulfa drugs are the antibacterial sulfonamides, which contain sulfur. Penicillins and cephalosporins are not sulfonamides; they are beta-lactam antibiotics whose ring systems also contain sulfur.

book_ref.quote: Sulfa drugs (the antibacterial sulfonamides) contain sulfur

blocks.prompt: 54 How are sulfur dyes made? Name two examples.
blocks.explanation: By thionation (sulfurization) of organic compounds containing nitro or amino groups; the dyes contain sulfur linkages and give black, brown, khaki, blue and green colours. Examples: sulfur black 1, sulfur blue (also sulfur brilliant green).

book_ref.quote: Sulfur dyes are synthesised by the process of thionation or sulfurization

blocks.prompt: 55 Give two uses of sulfur compounds as odorants or fragrances.
blocks.explanation: (i) Mercaptans give odour to natural gas. (ii) Thioterpineol is the key ingredient in the aroma of grapefruit; cis-galbanum oxathiane is used in fine fragrances, soaps, shampoos and shower gels.

book_ref.quote: Mercaptans are used to give odour to natural gas

blocks.prompt: 56 Describe the structure of the sulphuric acid molecule.
blocks.explanation: H₂SO₄ is tetrahedral around sulfur, with two S−O bonds (each to an OH group) and two S=O bonds. Sulfur is in the +6 state.

book_ref.quote: It has tetrahedral structure with two S−O and two S=O bonds

blocks.prompt: 57 Why is SO₂ from pyrite purified in the contact process? How is arsenic oxide removed?
blocks.explanation: Dust, vapours and arsenic oxide affect the efficiency of the catalyst. In the arsenic purifier, gelatinous Fe(OH)₃ on shelves absorbs it: As₂O₃ + 2Fe(OH)₃ → 2FeAsO₃ + 3H₂O.

book_ref.quote: In an arsenic purifier, gelatinous ferric hydroxide Fe(OH)₃

blocks.prompt: 58 Write the balanced equation for heating iron pyrite in excess air in the contact process.
blocks.explanation: Iron pyrite is FeS₂: 4FeS₂(s) + 11O₂(g) → 2Fe₂O₃(s) + 8SO₂(g). Check: O on the right = 6 + 16 = 22 = 11 O₂.

book_ref.quote: for iron pyrite, FeS₂, it is 4FeS₂(s) + 11O₂(g) → 2Fe₂O₃(s) + 8SO₂(g)

blocks.prompt: 59 State the conditions used in the contact tower.
blocks.explanation: Purified SO₂ and air are preheated to 420–450 °C and fed at 1–2 atm pressure over vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) catalyst: SO₂ + ½O₂ ⇌ SO₃, ΔH = −98.98 kJ mol⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: Purified SO₂ and air, preheated at 420 °C– 450 °C

blocks.prompt: 60 Calculate the heat released when 4.0 mol of SO₂ is converted into SO₃ in the contact tower (ΔH = −98.98 kJ mol⁻¹).
blocks.explanation: Heat released = 4.0 × 98.98 = 395.9 kJ (≈ 396 kJ); ΔH for 4.0 mol = −395.9 kJ.

book_ref.quote: these gases come in contact with vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) catalyst

blocks.prompt: 61 Write the equations for the formation of oleum and for its reaction with water.
blocks.explanation: SO₃ dissolves in sulphuric acid: H₂SO₄(l) + SO₃(g) → H₂S₂O₇(l) (oleum). Oleum with water: H₂S₂O₇(l) + H₂O(l) → 2H₂SO₄(l), giving acid of adjustable concentration.

book_ref.quote: Oleum undergoes a reaction with water to make a highly concentrated solution

blocks.prompt: 62 Why should concentrated sulphuric acid be kept in a closed bottle?
blocks.explanation: It is hygroscopic and readily absorbs water vapour from the air, which dilutes it. It is also highly corrosive and causes chemical burns, so it must be handled carefully.

book_ref.quote: Sulphuric acid is soluble in water and hygroscopic in nature

blocks.prompt: 63 Give four physical properties of sulphuric acid.
blocks.explanation: Colourless, odourless, viscous liquid; melting point 10 °C; boiling point 290 °C; specific gravity 1.83 g/cm³ at 15 °C (molar mass 98.08 g/mol).

book_ref.quote: Table 12.5 Physical properties of Sulphuric acid

blocks.prompt: 64 Why can sulphuric acid be used as a non-aqueous protic solvent?
blocks.explanation: It self-ionizes: H₂SO₄ + H₂SO₄ ⇌ H₃SO₄⁺ + HSO₄⁻, K = 2.7 × 10⁻⁴. This constant is greater than that of water, so it can act as a non-aqueous protic solvent.

book_ref.quote: The equilibrium constant value is greater than that of water

blocks.prompt: 65 Why is HSO₄⁻ a much weaker acid than H₂SO₄?
blocks.explanation: The first ionization H₂SO₄ + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + HSO₄⁻ has pKa1 = −2 (strong acid). The second, HSO₄⁻ + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + SO₄²⁻, has a positive pKa2 = 1.92, so HSO₄⁻ is a far weaker acid.

book_ref.quote: But hydrogensulfate (HSO₄¹⁻) is a far weaker acid due to a positive pKa2 value

blocks.prompt: 66 What is the carbon snake? Write the equation.
blocks.explanation: When concentrated H₂SO₄ dehydrates table sugar, a black porous carbon mass, the carbon snake, rises out: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → 12C(s) + 11H₂O(g) + H₂SO₄(aq).

book_ref.quote: a black porous carbon mass called carbon snake

blocks.prompt: 67 How is hydrogen chloride gas prepared from sodium chloride? Give the equation.
blocks.explanation: By the reaction of sodium chloride with sulphuric acid: NaCl(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → NaHSO₄(s) + HCl(g).

book_ref.quote: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) gas, is formed when sulphuric acid reacts with sodium chloride

blocks.prompt: 68 How does the reaction of zinc with dilute sulphuric acid differ from that with concentrated sulphuric acid?
blocks.explanation: See the table.

book_ref.quote: Zinc gives Zn²⁺, not Fe²⁺, and two H₂SO₄ are needed

blocks.prompt: 69 Sulphuric acid is not a typical oxidising agent, yet hot concentrated acid oxidises copper. Explain.
blocks.explanation: The SO₄²⁻ anion is stable and only weakly oxidising. Hot concentrated acid becomes a moderately strong oxidiser due to high temperature, high H⁺ concentration and nascent oxygen: Cu + 2H₂SO₄ → SO₂ + 2H₂O + SO₄²⁻ + Cu²⁺.

book_ref.quote: However hot concentrated sulphuric acid is a moderately strong oxidising agent

blocks.prompt: 70 Why is sulphuric acid called the king of chemicals?
blocks.explanation: It is used in a huge number of industries (fertilizers, metal extraction, refining, paper, explosives, paints, food, batteries) and its consumption is an indicator of the industrial progress of a country.

book_ref.quote: its consumption is an indicator of the industrial progress of a country

blocks.prompt: 71 Name two fertilizers made with the help of sulphuric acid.
blocks.explanation: (i) Single superphosphate, Ca(H₂PO₄)₂, from fluorapatite Ca₅(PO₄)₃F (phosphoric acid also forms). (ii) Ammonium sulfate, from the reaction of sulphuric acid with ammonia.

book_ref.quote: Fluorapatite (Ca₅(PO₄)₃F) to make single superphosphate

blocks.prompt: 72 Give four industrial uses of sulphuric acid other than fertilizers.
blocks.explanation: (i) Drying gases in industrial processes. (ii) Nitration in making explosives such as TNT. (iii) Making TiO₂ pigment for paints. (iv) Lead storage batteries (also metal extraction, pulp and paper, laboratory reagent).

book_ref.quote: It is used to dry gases in industrial processes
